newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Prominent Kuwaitis for ties with Yemen, Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Prominent Kuwaitis for ties with Yemen, Jordan.

text.p: Prominent Kuwaitis support normalisation of ties with 1990-91 Gulf crisis foes Jordan and Yemen but reject dealing with Sudan and the Palestinian Authority (PA), a poll published on Sunday said.

Al-Qabas daily said 79 percent of the 100 former ministers and parliamentarians, university professors and authors who took part in the poll favoured a resumption of ties with Iraq "after the fall of the regime of Saddam Hussein".

Kuwait does not have full links with a number of Arab governments which it accuses of supporting and sympathising with Iraq during its 1990-91 occupation of the Gulf Arab oil state. Generous financial aid to them was cut.

The poll showed that 61 percent supported a resumption of full ties with Jordan while 60 percent favoured relations with Yemen. Kuwait has turned down several overtures by both countries to normalise ties fully, although there have been signs of some improvement in relations.
Diplomats say such moves could prove to be unpopular although there are some officials and members of the ruling al-Sabah family who support it.
Kuwait last October was quick to say that it was too early to discuss normalisation of ties with Jordan after the prime ministers of the two states exchanged messages.
About 61 percent and 59 percent rejected normalisation of ties with the PA and Sudan respectively. Before Iraq's 1990 invasion, Kuwait was home to more than 400,000 Palestinians.
